text:
For most people, the **JBL Charge 6** is the best all-round pool and beach speaker. If you want something that floats, or you're throwing a bigger party, there are better picks below.

## Top picks

**1. JBL Charge 6 (best all-rounder), about $130–$150**
- **Water and sand:** IP68, so it's sealed against sand and survives being submerged. What Hi-Fi named it the best waterproof speaker overall.
- **Battery:** 20 hours, or 28 with Playtime Boost. It can also charge your phone.
- **Sound:** 40W, clear and powerful, with EQ in the app.
- **Catch:** None of these sources say it floats, so don't count on it bobbing back up if it falls in the pool.
- **Where to buy:** About $130 at Walmart, $150 at Amazon and $160 at Best Buy, through the buttons in [What Hi-Fi's guide](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) or [BestProducts' guide](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/).

**2. Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM (best for a pool you're actually in)**
- **Water and sand:** IP67, and it floats.
- **Sound:** 360°, so people get the same sound wherever they are around it. Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range pick.
- **Catch:** About 15 hours of battery, and it's not cheap.
- **Where to buy:** [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) or [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers), which link to Ultimate Ears, Amazon and B&H.

**3. JBL Boombox 4 (biggest party sound)**
- **Water:** Handles long submersion and floats. RTINGS' #1 waterproof speaker.
- **Battery:** Over 40 hours.
- **Sound:** Very loud and balanced.
- **Catch:** It's heavy and expensive, and it sounds muffled from the sides and back.
- **Where to buy:** [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), with links to Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart.

**4. Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 (best budget), about $65**
- **Water and sand:** IP67, and it floats.
- **Size and sound:** Softball-sized and tough, with 360° sound.
- **Battery:** 13–14 hours.
- **Catch:** No app, and limited bass.
- **Where to buy:** [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) lists it at $65 on Amazon and $67 at Walmart.

**5. JBL Grip (most packable), about $100**
- **Water and sand:** IP68.
- **Size:** Under 1 lb and can-shaped, so it fits a backpack bottle pocket.
- **Battery:** 12 hours.
- **Catch:** Good Housekeeping's tester notes the mesh body traps sand and dust.
- **Where to buy:** [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/), with links to Amazon, Walmart and Macy's.

**6. Soundcore Boom 2 Plus (big floating boombox deal), $200 with code AFSC20**
- **Price:** List price is $249.99. Code **AFSC20** took $49.99 off in a test on Oct 22, and it expires Dec 31.
- **Water:** IPX7 and floats. It has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach.
- **Sound and battery:** 100–140W, and 20 hours at half volume with the lights off.
- **Catch:** Heavy, at 3.8 kg (about 8.4 lb).
- **Where to buy:** [Soundcore's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus). This is an affiliate link from the deal site Dealectric, which earns a commission at no extra cost to you. Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus).

## Beach and pool tips
- **For the beach,** choose IP67 or IP68. The "6" means sand-tight. IPX7 speakers have no dust protection.
- **Rinse it with fresh water after use.** IP ratings don't cover corrosion from salt or chlorine ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)).
- **Before charging,** close the port flaps and let the speaker dry fully ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/)).

**Quick pick:** Choose the Charge 6 for the beach, the EPICBOOM if it might end up in the pool, and the Wonderboom 4 if you're on a budget.
